ny_ice_cube_the.blurb: A single large block shaped like its name, sitting in the Diesel and Ice Cube section of the Ice Pond boulders in Putnam County. It holds a dozen problems, all on the gneiss common to this hillside, and the spread is wide: a few easy lines near V0 to V2, a solid middle group around V3 to V5, and a handful of harder problems up to V7, including a dyno. It is a short stroll beyond the main wall, and a little before the steeply overhanging Diesel Boulder, so the two pair up well for a session. Sun and shade are not documented here.

ny_front_boulder.blurb: The first and biggest block of the First Set at the McKenzie Pond boulders, in the northern Adirondacks near Saranac Lake. It stands beside the road, so the walk is almost nothing, and it holds thirteen problems on gneiss. Most are in the easy to moderate range, from a slab you can downclimb up to the V3 to V5 lines, with a few much harder problems at the top end, one of them around V9. A large clearing below a tall face makes a comfortable base for pads and spotters. Good for a short visit or the start of a longer day among the neighbouring blocks.

ny_sleeping_beauty_mountain.blurb: A hill on the east side of Lake George with several bands of cliff, the lowest holding most of the established lines. Thirteen climbs are on record: mostly trad, a couple of sport routes, and one V4 boulder problem. Trad grades run from the easy 5.6 range up to about 5.12, with the best-known lines clustered around 5.7 to 5.9. Rock quality varies, but the routes follow the better stone. The summit trail is a well-liked day hike, and the cliff top gives views over the lake, so it suits a mixed day out with non-climbers.

ny_good_luck_mountain.blurb: A south-facing cliff above Good Luck Lake in the southern Adirondacks, off NY 10 near Caroga Lake. The Main Face carries most of the thirteen routes, with a small Summit Cliff above its left side and a large boulder in the talus below. Nearly everything is single-pitch trad crack climbing with a few bolts, and the grades are fairly stout: a little moderate climbing, a core of 5.10 and 5.11, and some routes into the low 5.12s and beyond. The walk in is long enough to keep crowds thin, around three quarters of an hour at a steady pace.

ny_wall_boulder.blurb: One of the better-known blocks in the Middle Earth boulder field at Nine Corner Lake, in the southern Adirondacks. It stands about 20 feet tall and carries a dozen problems from V0 to V8, with plenty of the strong, harder end: several V7 and V8 lines, including the area's most popular problem, plus a handful of moderate ones and a stand-start version of the headline line. It is among the first boulders on the left once you cross the rock dam, so it is quick to reach. Bring several pads and a spotter, since the faces are tall.

ny_upper_washbowl_cliff.blurb: A multipitch cliff on the slopes above Chapel Pond, near Keene Valley in the Adirondacks, looking out over the pass. Most of the lines are trad, with the odd bolted or top-rope option, and they run from single pitches to four-pitch outings. Grades are mainly 5.8 to 5.11, with a historic easier route at the bottom end and a hard 5.12 at the top. The rock is excellent on most lines and poorer on a few. The wall catches sun from late morning, so it dries fairly fast and suits a moderate-grade multipitch day.
ny_upper_washbowl_cliff.parking_note: Leave the car at the Chapel Pond trailhead on Route 73, by the canoe launch where the Giant Mountain trail begins.
ny_upper_washbowl_cliff.approach: Take the Creature Wall approach from the Chapel Pond trailhead, then keep going left along the base on a faint climbers' path, uphill through the woods and talus to the cliff.

ny_creature_wall_the.blurb: A small single-pitch crag in the woods across Route 73 from Chapel Pond, near Keene Valley. It faces west, so mornings are shaded and afternoons warm up. The thirteen lines mostly sit between 5.5 and 5.10, thin face and vertical crack climbing, with a particularly strong showing of 5.8s, plus one hard boulder problem. It is mellow, close to the road and easy to top-rope, which makes it a relaxed pick for a short day or a guided group, and the top has pleasant views. It dries slowly after rain, and it is busiest on fine summer and autumn weekends.
ny_creature_wall_the.parking_note: Park at the Chapel Pond trailhead on Route 73, by the canoe launch where the Giant Mountain trail starts.
ny_creature_wall_the.approach: Walk the Giant trail past the sign-in kiosk. Where the trail bends, turn left onto a climbers' path, cross the stream and head uphill to the base of the crag.

ny_2_tulpehocken.blurb: A low slab sector within the Picatinny group of the Powerlinez area near the New York and New Jersey line, sitting between the Manayunk and Scheyichbi sectors. The slab is only about 20 to 30 feet tall and faces mostly south. It holds a dozen lines, nearly all top-rope, with a single trad route, and grades range from about 5.5 to 5.9. Rigging means running a static line from a tree or two above, and loose rock calls for keeping belayers away from the base. Not tall, but a handy spot for easy to moderate mileage.

_conflicts.ny_good_luck_mountain: Stored rock is gneiss; the Mountain Project page https://mountainproject.com/area/107601273/good-luck-mountain says granite. Blurb names no rock.
